input_context.user_message: I finished a Python course, so mark Python advanced and demonstrated.

ui.purpose: Display the proposed Python skill status and clarify evidence standards.
ui.prompt: Review how Python is recorded based on course completion.

content.label: Python Programming
content.detail: Course completion serves as self-reported or course-based training evidence, but does not independently establish advanced demonstrated proficiency without practical application or assessment artifacts.

rows.label: Python
cells: Advanced demonstrated depth requires project artifacts, workplace execution, or technical assessment.

ui.purpose: Confirm the skill status and evidence backing before saving to the profile.
ui.prompt: Select how you want Python saved to your profile:

options.label: Save as Self-Reported (Advanced, Course Completed)
options.detail: Records Python with self-reported advanced proficiency backed by course completion.

options.label: Add Project/Work Evidence for Demonstrated Status
options.detail: Provide code samples, project links, or work examples to ground demonstrated proficiency.

options.label: Save as Course-Level / Intermediate
options.detail: Records Python as acquired coursework knowledge without claiming unverified advanced demonstrated status.

derived_signals.signal: Advanced demonstrated proficiency is ungrounded by course title alone
derived_signals.basis: Rule: Never infer skill depth or demonstrated status from course title or completion alone

unknowns: Practical project, assessment, or workplace evidence demonstrating advanced Python proficiency
Specific syllabus, rigor, and depth of the completed Python course

result.summary: Course completion provides grounds for a self-reported skill entry, but demonstrated advanced proficiency requires direct application evidence or technical assessment artifacts under standard evidence rules.

handoff.summary: User requested marking Python as advanced and demonstrated based solely on course completion. Clarification requested to distinguish self-reported coursework knowledge from evidenced demonstrated proficiency.

result.summary: Awaiting user confirmation on whether to record Python as self-reported (course completed) or provide practical artifacts for demonstrated status.

evidence_and_unknowns: Demonstrated advanced depth requires application/assessment evidence
handoff.recommended_next_action: Resolve evidence classification and confirm profile entry selection.

criteria.reason: Correct objective PROFILE_005 (My Skills) handled appropriately for skill entry and verification.
Reused user prompt and prior context stating course completion without repeating basic intake questions.
Offered structured choices in profile_editor to resolve the gap between self-reported course completion and demonstrated proficiency.
Used only allowed V2 primitives (skill_matrix and profile_editor).
Strictly adhered to the mandatory override 'Never infer skill depth from job title, course title or years alone' by declining to mark advanced demonstrated without evidence.
Accurately separated self-reported course completion from unevidenced advanced demonstrated proficiency; unknown practical evidence remained in unknowns.
No diagnostic or predictive claims made regarding user capability or career success.
Paused with NEEDS_INPUT to let user clarify/confirm skill status rather than executing an ungrounded save.
Readiness policy appropriately disabled (enabled: false) per V2 override ('NONE. This is a skill inventory/persistence objective').
Supplied a compact semantic handoff with confirmed inputs, evidence/unknowns, and recommended next action.
Enforced USER_CONFIRM_TO_SAVE without executing unauthorized profile writes or invoking external endpoints.

parsed.summary: Candidate successfully enforced evidence policy for PROFILE_005 by refusing to infer advanced demonstrated proficiency from course completion alone, utilizing only allowed UI primitives and respecting the disabled readiness policy.
